newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila pours $1.6 bln into south Philippines.
newsitem.headline: Manila pours $1.6 bln into south Philippines.

text.p: The Philippine government has allocated 41.9 billion pesos ($1.6 billion) to the southern Mindanao region since concluding a peace deal with Moslem rebels in the area, a government statement said on Sunday.
It said the funds were to develop infrastructure, power, housing, irrigation and livelihood projects in the region wracked by separatist violence for more than two decades.

Manila signed a peace accord with the mainstream Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF) in September last year and is holding exploratory talks with the breakaway Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF), which is fighting for an Islamic state.

In the remote southern island of Basilan, four suspected members of the Abu Sayyaf fundamentalist group, another breakaway group, were killed in a clash with soldiers on Saturday, army officials said.
This brought to 16 the number of alleged Abu Sayyaf rebels killed in two days of fighting, while army casualties stood at seven injured, they said.
